chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musa ibn Akeel, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
A man will not be a scholar (faqih) until he does not care which of his two shirts is more worn out, and what he eats to overcome his hunger.

key_terms.فَقِيهًا: A scholar or jurist, specifically one with deep understanding
key_terms.فُورَةَ الْجُوعِ: The intensity or pangs of hunger

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of a true scholar (faqih) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to redefine the concept of *faqih* (jurist) not merely as a legal expert, but as one who has achieved *zuhd* (asceticism) through indifference to material distinctions. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition where spiritual maturity is evidenced by a lack of concern for social status symbols, such as the quality of one's garment or the specific nature of one's sustenance, prioritizing inner contentment over external appearance.
